items.excerpt: Baylor College of Medicine's GluePlex workflow combines AI protein-structure prediction with physics-based modeling to predict how molecular glues bind VAV1 and CRBN without experimental structures, yielding compounds that degrade VAV1 and suppress T-cell activation (Nature Communications).

Tohoku University's AIMR proposes PhysMat AI, a framework that builds physical laws into materials-discovery AI as priors, descriptors, constraints and verifiers so predictions for catalysts, solid-state electrolytes and hydrogen storage become interpretable and experimentally testable (Advanced Functional Materials).

NYU researchers trained a graph neural network on 1.1M+ tautomeric states from the Cambridge Structural Database; it screened 4.6 million drug-like compounds in 3.2 hours on one GPU and flagged 126 of 5,075 protein ligands with likely wrong hydrogen positions (Chemical Science).

Medical University of Innsbruck's xECG, an xLSTM-based ECG foundation model trained on ~8 million ECGs from 1.7 million patients, outperforms rival models across classification, regression and survival tasks and handles 12-lead, long-term and smartwatch recordings; the team also released the BenchECG benchmark (npj Digital Medicine).

IDIBELL, Barcelona Supercomputing Center and ISGlobal built ChromAgeNet, a convolutional neural network that reads 3D chromatin images of mouse blood stem cell nuclei to classify young vs. aged cells (~77% accuracy) and flag chromatin signatures of aging for rejuvenation screening (Aging Cell).

UCSF and University of Michigan paired stimulated Raman histology with the FastGlioma AI system and ML models to predict where glioblastoma will recur after surgery, localizing recurrence within 5-10 mm of sampled tissue and beating conventional pathology (Science Advances).

A PNAS Nexus study tested 21 large language models on judging cooperation with people of good or bad reputation: models agreed on helping 'good' people but diverged on 'bad' ones (Gemma 2 and Llama 3.1 endorsed shunning), with judgments shifting by recipient gender and culture.

KAIST, UNIST and POSTECH built a neuromorphic reservoir-computing chip that stacks ion-gated transistor layers with fast and slow responses to recognize motion over time, reaching >90% accuracy on moving handwritten digits in simulation and staying stable for 55 months (Advanced Materials).

Cambridge's open-source Tessera AI model maps smallholder crops across Senegal from satellite imagery with 84% accuracy using limited training data, 28% better than competing models at low compute cost (Environmental Research: Food Systems).

Terra Quantum and Swiss lab Empa developed an AI model that predicts 3D temperature fields and melt-pool boundaries in laser welding within milliseconds, replacing slow physics simulations for process control.

A Harvard study finds LLMs judge trustworthiness and competence from facial appearance like humans do, with even stronger appearance bias than people on competence, and none of the tested models declined the biased judgments.

Ginkgo Datapoints and Apheris named AbbVie, argenx, Lundbeck and Takeda as founding members of a federated consortium building the largest standardized antibody-developability dataset, designed explicitly for training ML models that predict manufacturability risk (data access early 2027).
